Always test grain after a join: count(*) vs count(distinct primary_key). If they differ, you have fan-out.
NOT IN (subquery) returns zero rows if the subquery has any NULL. Use NOT EXISTS.
Every model in the dbt project ends with {{ audit_columns() }}. It's how you trace which run loaded what.
Fix metrics in the canonical dbt model, not in the Tableau calc. Otherwise every dashboard inherits the same bug.
SELECT * is cheap in OLTP and expensive in OLAP. Columnar storage rewards projecting only what you need.
Use severity: warn when introducing new tests. Harden to error after the data has proven clean.
PySpark transformations are lazy. Only an action (.show(), .collect(), .write()) triggers execution.
Slim CI for dbt: dbt build -s state:modified+. Only builds changed models + their downstream.
Broadcast small dim tables explicitly: /*+ BROADCAST(dim) */. The planner gets it wrong on bigger sources.
Surrogate keys built from md5(NULL || …) collapse all NULL-rows to the same key. Always use a guaranteed-unique column.
Idempotency is non-negotiable. Same input → same output, every retry. MERGE, not INSERT.
CDC tables (accounts, jobs, etc.) need WHERE __is_deleted = false. Missing it = production correctness bug.
OPTIMIZE compacts files; ZORDER sorts within. Use both regularly on hot tables.
When stakeholder says 'real-time', ask 'what latency is actually fine?'. 5-minute micro-batch saves 10× cost vs full streaming.
Data contracts move the failure left: catch the schema change at PR time, not at 9pm Friday.
Use {{ ref() }}, never hardcoded paths. The whole dbt DAG depends on it.
Naming convention beats cleverness. fct_jobs > jobs_v3_final.
Test for what you'd be embarrassed by, not what's easy to test. Edge cases > happy paths.
Read query plans bottom-up. The lowest exchange is usually the bottleneck.
Document the grain in every fact model. 'One row per (job_id, contractor_id, event_ts)' — write it.
